title: memQ and Infleqtion Partner to Advance Interoperability in Networked Quantum Computing

content:
memQ, a Chicago-based quantum networking technology company, and Infleqtion (NYSE: INFQ), a developer of neutral-atom quantum computing and sensing systems, have signed a memorandum of understanding to explore interoperability between their quantum networking, computing and software technologies.

Announced November 19, 2026, the collaboration will focus on validating and certifying compatibility between memQ’s extensible Quantum Network Architecture (xQNA), Infleqtion’s Sqale quantum computer and its Superstaq quantum software platform.

The companies aim to develop technology that could enable multiple quantum computing systems to operate together through quantum networks, creating more flexible computing configurations and supporting the development of distributed quantum processing.

The initiative draws on the clustering model used in high-performance computing (HPC), where multiple computing systems work together to process complex workloads.

Unlike conventional computers, quantum systems face significant technical challenges when attempting to share quantum information across existing data networks. Quantum states are highly sensitive to disturbances, making reliable connections between separate quantum processors difficult.

Quantum networking technologies are being developed to address those limitations and enable computing resources to be distributed across interconnected systems.

“As a leader in quantum computing, we realize that building truly useful systems means understanding how different technologies can work together,” said Pranav Gokhale, chief technology officer of Infleqtion.

“Interoperability is essential as our industry moves toward broader commercial deployments. Our collaboration with memQ reflects our shared commitment to building an ecosystem that moves end-users closer to confident adoption across their enterprise.”

Under the memorandum of understanding, memQ and Infleqtion will pursue interoperability validation between their respective technologies, with an emphasis on supporting modular expansion and distributed quantum computing configurations.

memQ’s xQNA portfolio provides optical connectivity and control technologies designed to link different types of quantum systems while preserving the quantum states required for computation.

Infleqtion’s Sqale platform uses neutral-atom technology for quantum computing, while its Superstaq software provides tools for developing and optimizing quantum applications.

The collaboration is intended to explore how these technologies can work together to expand the range of potential quantum computing applications.

“Quantum computing is advancing rapidly, but if the HPC market is any indicator, the needs of end users will require even greater configuration and deployment flexibility,” said Charles Foley, CEO of memQ.

“Quantum networking provides a path to bringing multiple systems together and expanding the ability to leverage quantum resources across more workloads.”

The announcement comes as industry forecasts point to substantial growth in quantum computing investment.

According to IDC, worldwide customer spending on quantum computing is projected to increase from $4.2 billion in 2025 to $27.5 billion by 2030.

Heather West, global quantum research lead at IDC, identified connectivity and the development of a viable technology ecosystem as important challenges facing the industry’s expansion.

The companies also highlighted the importance of compatibility with existing enterprise computing environments.

Kevin Moran, CEO of HPC systems integrator System Fabric Works, said organizations exploring quantum computing need confidence that the technology can fit into their established operational models.

The agreement reflects efforts to develop an interoperable quantum computing ecosystem rather than relying exclusively on standalone systems.

However, the announcement represents an agreement to pursue technical validation and certification, not a completed demonstration of interoperable distributed quantum computing.

The companies did not disclose financial terms or a timeline for completing the interoperability work.

memQ develops optical connectivity and quantum networking technologies designed to support modular and distributed quantum computing architectures.

Infleqtion develops neutral-atom quantum technologies for computing, sensing, networking and security. Its product portfolio includes quantum computers, optical clocks, radio-frequency receivers and inertial sensors, alongside its Superstaq software platform.

Infleqtion operates across the United States, Europe and Asia and serves government and commercial customers in industries including defense, energy, finance, telecommunications and aerospace.

The collaboration is intended to help establish technical foundations for connecting quantum computing systems as the industry works toward broader commercial deployment.
